notes_list.title: Cis vs Trans Alkene from Alkyne
notes_list.basic_overview: Partial reduction of alkynes can be controlled to produce either cis- or trans-alkenes.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Lindlar catalyst + H2 → cis-alkene. Na/NH3(l) or Li/NH3(l) → trans-alkene. Complete catalytic hydrogenation with excess H2 can continue to the alkane.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Partial reduction of alkynes can be controlled to produce either cis- or trans-alkenes. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
